extracted.intended_audience: applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and International Searching Authorities engaged in PCT international-phase processing
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for (a) amending claims under PCT Article 19/Rule 46 (including form, timing, content and statements) and (b) requesting and carrying out Supplementary International Searches under PCT Rule 45 bis (request content, fees, scope, unity and reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of patent documents (required elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing a patent document include: (A) the country or organization code and document number and kind code as given in WIPO Standard ST.16 or, if not indicated on that document, as provided in that Standard; (B) the name of the patentee or applicant (in capital letters, where appropriate, abbreviated); (C) the date of publication of the cited patent document or, in case of a corrected patent document, the date of issuance of the corrected patent document as referred to under INID code (48) of WIPO Standard ST.9 and, if provided on the document, the supplementary correction code as referred to under INID code (15); (D) where applicable, the pages, columns, lines or paragraph numbers where the relevant passages appear, or the relevant figures of the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples are provided showing full citation formats (e.g., JP 10-105775 A (NCR INTERNATIONAL INC.) 24 April 1998 (24.04.1998) paragraphs 26 to 30). Use the INID conventions and WIPO Standard ST.16 codes; specify precise locations (pages/columns/lines/figures) where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of WIPO Standard ST.16 for patent kinds
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify kinds of patent documents using the Standard Code for the Identification of Different Kinds of Patent Documents (WIPO Standard ST.16), which is subdivided into mutually exclusive groups characterizing patent documents, nonpatent literature (N) and restricted documents (X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Part 7.3 for examples of patent documents, alphabetical listing of issuing offices and samples of first pages. Use the correct kind letter groups corresponding to publication levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taking into account results of earlier search (PCT Rule 41)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant has requested under Rule 4.12 that an ISA take into account results of an earlier search and complied with Rule 12bis.1: (i) if the earlier search was by the same ISA or by the same Office acting as ISA, the ISA shall, to the extent possible, take those results into account; (ii) if the earlier search was by another ISA or by another Office, the ISA may take those results into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant provided copies (and translations where needed) of earlier search results and cited documents (excluding US patents/publications), the examiner shall take them into account; if not provided, taking them into account is at examiner discretion. Examiners are not bound by earlier searches; they perform a cursory review and then a more comprehensive inspection of cited references if warranted. The international search report forms do not indicate whether or to what extent earlier searches were taken into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of international-type searches in U.S. national practice
rubrics_metrics.description: An international-type search will be made in all national applications filed on and after June 1, 1978. Any national application may also have an international-type search report prepared at national examination upon specific written request and payment of the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP §1819 and 37 CFR are cited: the Patent Office does not require a prior formal report to obtain a search fee refund in a later-filed international application. When the applicant requests ISA/US to use earlier foreign search results, examiners should check Box VII of the PCT Request and follow instructions for taking earlier search results into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for Article 19 amendments (PCT Rule 46.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit for filing amendments under Article 19 is two months from transmittal of the international search report to the International Bureau and to the applicant by the ISA, or 16 months from the priority date, whichever expires later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment received by the IB after the time limit may be considered received on the last day of the time limit if it reaches the IB before technical preparations for international publication are completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to file Article 19 amendments (PCT Rule 46.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments made under Article 19 must be filed directly with the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not file Article 19 amendments with the receiving Office or the ISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of Article 19 amendments (PCT Rule 46.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application was filed in a language other than the language of publication, any amendment under Article 19 shall be in the language of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure amendments are in the publication language to be accepted and published with the international application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement under Article 19: format and content limits (PCT Rule 46.4 / Article 19(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement under Article 19(1) must be in the language of publication and shall not exceed 500 words if in English or if translated into English. The statement should be identified by a heading, preferably 'Statement under Article 19(1)'. It shall contain no disparaging comments on the international search report or relevance of citations; references to citations may be made only in connection with an amendment of that claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement is optional; it is published with the international application. It must be tied to specific amendments; general comments or disparaging remarks are prohibited. Statements not complying with requirements are not published nor communicated to designated Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of amendments (replacement sheets) and accompanying letter (PCT Rule 46.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments under Article 19 must be submitted as replacement sheet(s) containing a complete set of claims replacing all originally filed claims, accompanied by a letter which identifies the claims that differ, draws attention to differences between original and amended claims, identifies cancelled claims, and indicates the basis for the amendments in the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement sheets must contain clean text only (no marked-up text). All claims on replacement sheets must be numbered in Arabic numerals. Where a claim is cancelled, renumbering is not required but if renumbered they must be consecutive. The accompanying letter should state for each claim whether it is unchanged, cancelled, new, replaces one or more claims, is result of division, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative identification of claim differences (PCT Administrative Instructions Section 205)
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing amendments under Article 19 or Article 34(2)(b), the applicant shall indicate differences between claims as filed and claims as amended and, in connection with each claim in the international application, whether the claim is unchanged, cancelled, new, replaces one or more claims as filed, replaces one or more claims as previously amended, is result of division of a claim as filed/as previously amended, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identical indications for several claims may be grouped. Use Arabic numerals and consecutive renumbering if renumbering is performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to indicate specific basis for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The letter accompanying replacement sheets must indicate the basis for the amendments in the application as filed with specific references to particular parts of the application; non-specific indications such as 'see the description as filed' or 'see the claims as filed' are generally not considered sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise line/paragraph/drawing references so the examiner can assess whether amendments introduce subject-matter extending beyond the disclosure as filed. Examples illustrate acceptable phrasing (e.g., 'Basis for the amendment: Claim 1 ... basis found in original claims 2 and 4 as filed').

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional applicant statement explaining amendments (Article 19 statement distinctness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment may be accompanied by a brief statement explaining the amendment and indicating any impact on the description and drawings. That statement is published together with the international application and must refer to specific amendments; it must not exceed 500 words in English or translation into English, must not contain disparaging comments, and must be in the language of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate this statement from (a) the letter indicating differences and basis for amendments and (b) any statement required in a Demand for international preliminary examination. Identify the statement by 'Statement under Article 19(1)'. Non-compliant statements are neither published nor communicated to designated Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments must not extend beyond disclosure as filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments are not to go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed. While this requirement is not directly enforceable during Chapter I, failure to comply may have adverse consequences during international preliminary examination and in the national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure amendments have a clear and specific basis in the originally filed disclosure to avoid added-subject-matter objections later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary International Search (SIS) availability and purpose (Rule 45 bis general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The supplementary international search is an optional service allowing additional searches by one or more Supplementary International Searching Authorities (SISAs) during the international phase to reduce the risk of new prior art arising in the national phase by expanding linguistic and technical scope of search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesting SIS can be strategic to cover prior art in other languages/technical fields or from Offices where the applicant intends to enter the national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary search request timing and competent Authorities (PCT Rule 45 bis.1 & 45 bis.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may, at any time prior to the expiration of 22 months from the priority date, request a supplementary international search by an ISA competent under Rule 45 bis.9. Requests may be in respect of more than one such Authority. An Authority is competent if its preparedness to do so is stated in the applicable agreement under Article 16(3)(b), subject to limitations; the Authority that carried out the main international search under Article 16(1) shall not be competent to carry out the supplementary search for the same application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competence may have limitations (subject matter, total number of searches, claim limits). Verify applicable agreements and competence before requesting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of a supplementary search request (PCT Rule 45 bis.1(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplementary search request submitted to the International Bureau must indicate: (i) the name and address of applicant and agent (if any), the title of the invention, the international filing date and international application number; (ii) the International Searching Authority requested for the supplementary search; and (iii) where the application was filed in a language not accepted by that Authority, whether any translation furnished under Rule 12.3 or 12.4 is to form the basis of the supplementary international search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full contact details, precise identification of the Authority requested, and language/translation instructions to avoid processing delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accompanying materials for supplementary search requests (PCT Rule 45 bis.1(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, the request shall be accompanied by (i) a translation of the international application into a language accepted by the Authority if neither the filing language nor furnished translation is accepted by that Authority; and (ii) preferably, a copy of a sequence listing in electronic form complying with Administrative Instructions if required by the Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing translations and sequence listings at request time facilitates prompt handling and accurate searching by the SISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary search fees, payment and refunds (PCT Rule 45 bis.2 & 45 bis.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplementary search request is subject to a supplementary search handling fee payable to the International Bureau and each SISA may require a supplementary search fee payable for its service. Fees must be paid within one month from the date of receipt of the supplementary search request (amounts applicable on date of payment). The IB or Authority shall refund fees if the application is withdrawn or the request is considered not to have been submitted before documents are transmitted or before the Authority has started the search as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees may be paid in the currency set out in the Schedule or other currency prescribed by the IB; late payment and refund conditions are specified further below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checking, correction of defects and late payment (PCT Rule 45 bis.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau will promptly check whether the request complies with Rule 45 bis.1(b) and (c)(i) and invite the applicant to correct defects within one month. If supplementary search handling and search fees are not paid by the due time, the IB will invite payment with a late payment fee (50% of the supplementary search handling fee) within one month. Failure to correct defects or pay fees within the time limit results in the request being considered not submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly to IB invitations to avoid the request being declared not submitted. Late payment fee equals 50% of the handling fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents to be transmitted to the Authority specified for supplementary search (PCT Rule 45 bis.4(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: On finding requirements complied with, the IB shall transmit to the Authority specified for supplementary search copies of: (i) the supplementary search request; (ii) the international application; (iii) any sequence listing furnished; (iv) any translation to be used as basis; and, at same time or after later receipt, (v) the international search report and written opinion established under Rule 43 bis.1; (vi) any invitation by the ISA to pay additional fees under Article 17(3)(a); and (vii) any protest by the applicant under Rule 40.2(c) and decision thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On request of the Authority, the written opinion shall be translated into English by or under responsibility of the IB and transmitted within two months from receipt of the request; a copy is also sent to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start, basis and scope of the supplementary international search (PCT Rule 45 bis.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority specified for supplementary search shall start the search promptly after receipt of the specified documents, but may delay until it receives the ISR/written opinion or until expiration of 22 months from priority date. The search is carried out on the basis of the international application as filed or an accepted translation, taking due account of the ISR and written opinion if available. The Authority may exclude claims not subject to the international search, may decide not to establish a supplementary search report if an Article 17(2)(a) declaration applies, and must cover at least the documentation indicated in the applicable agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Authority may restrict the search to certain claims; if exclusions or restrictions apply they must be indicated in the supplementary international search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention in supplementary search (PCT Rule 45 bis.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Authority finds non-compliance with the unity requirement it shall: (i) establish the supplementary search report on parts relating to the 'main invention' (first-mentioned); (ii) notify applicant of its opinion and reasons; and (iii) inform applicant of possibility of requesting review within the time limit. The applicant may request review within one month and may be charged a review fee; the review shall not be carried out solely by the person who made the decision. Outcomes: opinion fully justified; partially unjustified (may proceed to search additional parts); entirely unjustified (search all parts and refund the review fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should act promptly if disputing non-unity findings; review processes and potential fee refunds are available as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary international search report timing and content (PCT Rule 45 bis.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority specified for supplementary search shall, within 28 months from the priority date, establish the supplementary international search report or make a declaration that no report will be established. Reports and declarations shall be in the language of publication. The supplementary report need not cite documents already cited in the ISR except when needed in conjunction with other documents not cited in the ISR, and may contain explanations regarding citations and the scope of the supplementary search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules applicable to preparation of the ISR apply mutatis mutandis, with some exceptions noted in the Rules. Use the language of publication and follow the citation conventions described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal and legal effect of the supplementary international search report (PCT Rule 45 bis.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority shall transmit one copy of the supplementary international search report (or declaration of none) on the same day to the IB and one copy to the applicant. Subject to certain paragraphs, Article 20(1) and relevant rules shall apply as if the supplementary report were part of the international search report. However, the supplementary report need not be taken into account by the IPEA for its written opinion or international preliminary examination report if received after it has begun drawing up that opinion or report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely transmission is important to ensure the supplementary report is considered by downstream authorities; late arrival may limit its practical effect for international preliminary examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and competence rules for Supplementary International Searching Authorities (PCT Rule 45 bis.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Authority is competent to carry out supplementary searches if its preparedness is stated in the applicable agreement under Article 16(3)(b), subject to limitations and conditions in that agreement. The Authority that carried out the main international search under Article 16(1) shall not be competent to carry out supplementary searches for that application. Limitations may include subject-matter restrictions, caps on total supplementary searches, or maximum claims searched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should select Authorities aware of these limitations and consistent with strategic national-phase plans; check agreements under Article 16(3)(b) for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical benefits and strategic considerations for requesting SIS
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesting a supplementary international search reduces the risk of new prior art emerging in the national phase by expanding linguistic and technical coverage, and may allow searching in a State where the applicant expects to enter national phase later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider SIS when the main ISA may have limited linguistic/technical coverage relative to relevant prior art domains or when planning entry into particular national phases.
